answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making trust grow like a vine rather than appear on demand. New identities enter through a single narrow inlet: they must complete small verifiable tasks for established agents, earning endorsements that decay over time. Each endorsement is staked, so if the newcomer cheats, the voucher loses stake too. A sybil farmer must therefore fund months of honest work across many terraces of the trust graph, and one fraud collapses the whole vine, wiping the investment.
